title: Test your OLTP vs OLAP basics

questions.q: A shop's till and website record each sale the moment it happens. Which job is that?
options: OLAP, because it deals with sales data
OLTP, because it records one transaction at a time
Neither, because only a warehouse can store sales
OLAP, because it needs to be fast
questions.explain: That's OLTP, the database behind your app. It records orders, payments and sign-ups one at a time, fast and correctly.

questions.q: Your finance team wants a report that adds up millions of past orders. Why is running it on the live shop database a bad idea?
options: It would delete the old orders
The report would be too inaccurate to trust
It can be slow and can block other transactions, like customers paying
Live databases refuse to answer any report at all
questions.explain: Microsoft says reports that add up millions of transactions are very resource-intensive for an OLTP system. They can be slow and can block other transactions, though it notes exceptions such as a well-planned schema.

questions.q: The dashboard is fed by an overnight copy, so it is a day behind. Which question should still go to the live OLTP side?
options: Is this item in stock right now?
Which region sold the most this year?
How did revenue trend over the last 12 months?
Which products sold best last quarter?
questions.explain: A day-old copy is fine for monthly reports. For something like "is this in stock right now?", it's wrong, so that question goes to the OLTP side.

questions.q: Why can a column store add up one field across millions of records so quickly?
options: It keeps every full record together, so it reads whole rows at once
It reads the whole table, then discards the fields it does not need
It copies every row to a second system before it answers
It keeps each field together, so it only reads the columns it needs
questions.explain: A column store keeps each field together, so adding up one field is quick. A row store keeps each record together, so finding one order is quick.

questions.q: So which should a growing company pick, OLTP or OLAP?
options: OLAP alone, since it can answer every question
Usually both, with data copied from the first into the second
OLTP alone, since big reports are safe to run on the live app
Whichever has the bigger brand name
questions.explain: AWS says most companies use both together. The better question is usually how to connect them, because they do different jobs.
